newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's major privatizations scheduled for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's major privatizations scheduled for 1997.

text.p: The following are the main Brazilian privatizations scheduled for 1997.

* State mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) beginning in March with the sale of a 40-45 percent block of voting shares. The remainder will be offered to employees and to foreign and domestic investors in subsequent auctions.
* Sao Paulo state power utilities beginning in the second half of 1997. Companhia Paulista de Forca e Luz, or (CPFL), is expected to be the first of the state's power firms to be sold off.

* A 28 percent stake in Rio de Janeiro power utility Light that remained in the hands of the federal government after a larger share was sold to private foreign and local investors in May. The date of the selloff will depend on market performance.
* Furnas and Eletrosul, two of federally owned Eletrobras' power-generating units, and some of Eletrobras' 11 small hydroelectric and thermoelectric plants. No time given.
* Band B cellular phone service concessions in the first quarter.
* Telebras system seen partially sold off in 1997, with the sales of long-distance unit Embratel and the biggest regional telecoms after the firm's subsidiaries are split into four regional units.
* Itajai, Cabedelo, Porto Velho and Laguna ports beginning in the first half. The government also plans to sell the ports of Recife, Maceio and Manaus next year.

* A 30-year concession to operate the Northeast section of Brazil's federal railway network sometime in the first quarter. The Northeast stretch will be the last of the six rail sections to be privatized.
